summary: Everyone takes the COMPLIT 101 gateway (also the WIM course), COMPLIT 121, 122 and 123, and the COMPLIT 199 capstone, then either completes the electives or the Comparative Literature and Philosophy subplan. Without a subplan you need 40 units of electives, at least 15 of them COMPLIT courses (not COMPLIT 194), for 65 units in all. The Philosophy subplan needs COMPLIT 181, PHIL 80, a 170-series and a 180-series course, two history of philosophy courses, its other listed courses and a capstone, for 66 units in all. Every course must be letter graded, with a C or better in the gateway and core courses. You check by hand the electives that form your approved focus, the courses on the Philosophy and Literature website, the second literary tradition, and for honors the GPA and thesis.

node.name: Remaining elective units in an approved intellectual focus

add.why: "The remaining courses should form a coherent intellectual focus requiring approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS). They may be drawn from Comparative Literature offerings, other literature departments, or other fields of interdisciplinary relevance." "Language classes taken for a letter grade (excluding conversational courses) and up to ten units of SLE or COLLEGE courses taught at least partially by a Comparative Literature Department faculty member may be counted". The student moves the approved courses in.

node.name: Comparative Literature and Philosophy Subplan Capstone Experience

children.name: Philosophy and Literature Capstone Seminar
children.desc: Students should discuss their choice of capstone seminar with the Director of Undergraduate Studies and the Faculty Advisor for Philosophy.

children.name: Honors Thesis
children.desc: Only available if accepted into the Honors program: a minimum of 9 units (3 units per quarter), a thesis, and a presentation at the Honors Colloquium.

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc: A 5,000-word paper on philosophy and literature, written in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group, who approves the topic by the add/drop deadline.

add.why: The subplan's capstone, moved from the Capstone block: "Students should discuss their choice of capstone seminar with the Director of Undergraduate Studies"; the honors thesis option "is only available if accepted into the Honors program"; the topic paper requires "a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member ... the faculty member must approve the topic". Seminar and independent study are moved in by hand.
